subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Compared with a conscious response, a spinal reflex is:
options: Slower and decided by the brain
The same speed but uses more neurones
Faster because it bypasses conscious brain processing
questions.explain: Reflexes are faster than conscious responses because they do not pass through the conscious brain.

questions.q: After a sugary meal, blood glucose rises. The correct homeostatic response is for the pancreas to release:
options: Insulin, so cells take up glucose and the liver stores it as glycogen
ADH, so more water is reabsorbed
Glucagon, so the liver releases more glucose
Adrenaline, so the heart beats faster
questions.explain: High blood glucose triggers insulin release, causing cells to absorb glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, which hormone maintains the uterus lining in the second half of the cycle?
questions.explain: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterus lining; when its level falls, the lining breaks down and menstruation occurs.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: Which organ monitors and controls blood glucose concentration by releasing insulin and glucagon?
questions.explain: The pancreas detects blood glucose levels and secretes insulin or glucagon to keep them within normal limits.

questions.q: A scientist measures the reaction time of a person catching a falling ruler. This is testing the speed of a:
questions.explain: Catching a ruler requires the brain to process the stimulus and decide to react, so it tests a conscious response.

questions.q: Negative feedback in homeostasis works by:
options: Reinforcing a change so it grows larger
Detecting a change and triggering a response that reverses it back to normal
questions.explain: Negative feedback reverses changes: if a level rises too high, a response lowers it back towards the normal value.

questions.q: Type 1 diabetes is caused by:
options: The body's cells not responding to insulin
The kidneys failing to filter glucose
The pancreas not producing enough (or any) insulin
questions.explain: In Type 1 diabetes the pancreas produces little or no insulin, so it is usually treated with insulin injections.

questions.q: Which structure protects the relay neurones and passes impulses between the body and the brain?
questions.explain: The spinal cord, part of the CNS, contains relay neurones and carries impulses to and from the brain.

questions.q: What is the role of a relay neurone in the spinal cord during a reflex?
options: It connects the sensory neurone to the motor neurone
It releases hormones into the blood
questions.explain: Relay neurones link sensory and motor neurones within the CNS, allowing the reflex to bypass the conscious brain.

questions.q: Which neurone carries impulses from a receptor towards the central nervous system?
questions.explain: Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.

questions.q: In the menstrual cycle, a surge of which hormone triggers ovulation?
questions.explain: A surge in LH at around day 14 stimulates the release of an egg (ovulation).

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is associated with:
options: The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
A complete lack of a pancreas
Too much insulin being produced from birth
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: Urea, which is removed by the kidneys, is produced in the liver from the breakdown of excess:
questions.explain: The liver breaks down excess amino acids in a process called deamination, forming urea that the kidneys excrete.

questions.q: What does a receptor in the nervous system do?
options: Detects a stimulus such as light, heat or pressure
questions.explain: Receptors detect stimuli (changes in the environment) and convert them into electrical impulses.

questions.q: FSH (follicle stimulating hormone) acts to:
options: Cause an egg (in a follicle) to mature in the ovary
questions.explain: FSH, secreted by the pituitary gland, stimulates eggs to mature in the ovaries and triggers oestrogen release.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

questions.q: A motor neurone carries impulses:
options: From the CNS to an effector
From a receptor to the CNS
questions.explain: Motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors such as muscles or glands.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: Which hormone controls how much water is reabsorbed in the kidney tubules?
questions.explain: ADH increases the permeability of kidney tubules so more water is reabsorbed when the body is dehydrated.

questions.q: What two organs make up the central nervous system (CNS)?
questions.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, which coordinate the body's responses.

questions.q: How does the contraceptive pill (containing oestrogen/progesterone) prevent pregnancy?
options: It kills sperm directly in the uterus
It inhibits FSH so no eggs mature
questions.explain: The hormones in the pill inhibit FSH production, so no eggs mature and ovulation does not occur.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Biology (2017) specification; Coordination Control
